newsitem.title: USA: Cooper sees Q2 EPS $0.36 to $0.40/shr.
newsitem.headline: Cooper sees Q2 EPS $0.36 to $0.40/shr.

text.p: Cooper Companies Inc, a maker of specialty health care products and services, on Wednesday said it expects to earn $0.36 to $0.40 a share, including tax benefits of $0.02 a share, in its second quarter ending April 30.
In the year ago quarter, Cooper earned $0.24 a share.

For all of fiscal 1997, Cooper expects operating earnings to range from $1.45 to $1.55 a share versus $1.00 a share in fiscal 1996. With the tax benefit, earnings per share are expected to be between $1.60 and $1.70 per share versus $1.41.

In a statement delivered to shareholders at a recent meeting, Chief Executive Officer Thomas Bender said he expects revenue to grow at double-digit rates and operating earnings at mid-teen rates in the next several years.
Cooper's medium term business goals include 20 percent compounded revenue growth through 2000 and 40 percent earnings growth, excluding tax benefits, in each of the next two years.

Bender said he expects the company's CooperVision unit to produce revenue over $100 million and CooperSurgical to reach $50 million by 2000. Hospital Group of America's revenue should exceed $50 million in fiscal 1998, Bender estimated.
He said CooperSurgical will continue to be an aggressive consolidator in the gynecology device market through product and company acquisitions and marketing alliances.
Bender said the Hospital Group of America's emphasis on outpatient programs has boosted outpatient visits by 55 percent over one year ago.

Hospital Group of America now contributes positively to Cooper's operating results and going forward, it is expected to generate income from operations of more than 10 percent of revenue, Bender said.
